message_source_quote: The published white-bear method (Raman et al. 2026) extracted its stance vector from WSB's `directed_modulation` family, and its one self-written alternative (hold-vs-mention) **failed**. My contribution shows the direction is **bank-independent**
writeup_source_quote: The white-bear observation (Raman et al., 2026) is that a model represents "hold something in mind while writing" as a residual-stream direction separable from *what* is held; they extracted it from WSB's `directed_modulation` bank. I show the direction is bank-independent.

differences.what: message adds an extra verification (different stance verb 'imagine/don't-imagine' collapsing to the same axis, cosine 0.87) as further evidence for the novelty claim that it is the stance, not the wording, that carries the effect; this experiment and its interpretation are not mentioned anywhere in the write-up
differences.message_quote: I also verified that a different stance verb ("imagine/don't-imagine") collapses to the same axis (cosine 0.87), isolating that it is the suppression stance, not the wording, that carries the effect.

rationale: Both documents name Raman et al. 2026 explicitly as the source of the white-bear/directed_modulation stance direction and both frame the contribution identically: the method shows the direction is bank-independent and can be built from arbitrary self-written think/don't-think pairs, contrasted with the one published self-written attempt (hold-vs-mention) that failed. The message adds one extra piece of supporting evidence for novelty (the imagine/don't-imagine verb test) that does not appear in the write-up, otherwise the source treatment and novelty framing are equivalent (split: equal, with a minor 'more' addition).
